text:
B: Hiya. Can you hear me?
A: Yes, fine. I'm Jibin, near Bristol. Bradley Stoke.
B: Kerry. Bridgwater. So we're practically neighbours.
A: Practically. Forty minutes on the M5 if the Filton junction is not a disaster. Which it always is.
B: Ha. Yeah. What do you do, then? I'm guessing something with computers.
A: Embedded software. Aerospace. Flight-control verification, basically.
B: Right. Sounds like you'd be picky.
A: Er, it's a job where you have to be picky, to be honest. If I'm not picky, that's a problem.
B: Fair enough. I'm a painter and decorator, so I'm picky about different stuff.
A: Okay. Actually, maybe you can tell me something. We're in a new-build, four years, and the developer never fixed the snagging. There are cracks where the walls meet the ceiling, in almost every room. They said it's normal.
B: It is normal, to be fair. New-builds settle, the plaster dries out, you get hairline cracks along the joins. Everyone gets them.
A: But four years? It should have finished settling, surely.
B: Mostly, yeah. You rake them out, flexible filler, or decorator's caulk on the corners, sand it, then paint. Don't just slap emulsion over, it'll come back.
A: Caulk. Not normal filler?
B: On the corner joins, caulk, because it moves. Flat bits of wall, filler. That's what I'd do anyway, I've done about a hundred of them.
A: Okay. That makes sense, actually. I'd assumed it was structural.
B: If you can get a coin in it, ring someone. If it's a hairline, it's not.
A: Good test. Cheers.
B: No worries. Do you do your own decorating, then?
A: Er, I did one room. My wife says never again. I'm better with the thermostat. I have a smart system, every room separate, it saves quite a lot on the bills.
B: I rent, so I just put a jumper on.
A: Fair enough. Bridgwater, is that near Taunton? I go to the cricket at Taunton sometimes.
B: Yeah, twenty minutes. My son's dad lives there. Jayden goes every other weekend.
A: Okay. Does he play cricket? Your son?
B: No, football. Sunday league. I'm on the touchline every week shouting.
A: My son is twelve, he does nothing outside except complain. He wants a gaming PC.
B: Oh, Jayden's on about one of them. They're a fortune, aren't they.
A: They are if you buy the prebuilt ones. You're paying for the lights and the brand. If you choose the parts yourself, much better value. Graphics card is where you spend, the rest you can be sensible.
B: See, I wouldn't have a clue what any of that means.
A: I can tell you what to look for, if you like. Just quickly.
B: Go on then. Jayden'll think I'm a genius.
A: Basically, don't let him choose the—
